question.prompt: What is the measure of the acute angle formed by the hands of a clock at \(4{:}20\) a.m.?

solutions.explanation:
At \(4{:}20\), the minute hand points exactly to the \(4\). The hour hand has already moved partway from \(4\) toward \(5\).

The \(12\) hour marks divide a full turn equally, so neighboring marks are
\[
360^\circ\div12=30^\circ
\]
apart. The hour hand takes \(60\) minutes to move through this gap. In \(20\) minutes it moves one-third of the gap, or
\[
\frac{20}{60}\cdot30^\circ=10^\circ.
\]
Thus the hands are \(\boxed{10^\circ}\) apart. This angle is acute, so the answer is choice \(\text{D}\).
solutions.title: Track the hour hand past 4
